result:
Round 2 appended. Three files changed since round 1 — `preamble.tex`, `p1.tex`, `p5.tex`, one hunk each. `main.tex`, `p2`, `p3`, `p4` are byte-identical, so round 1's verification of Ex. 3.2–3.9 carries over.

**Mechanical re-checks** — recompiled from the shipped sources: exit 0, zero overfull/underfull boxes, no undefined references, 11 pages. The shipped `main.pdf` extracts to text identical to my rebuild, so it is genuinely built from the shipped sources. Lint clean on p1–p5 and `final --final`. Paper sub-answers now 527/569/543/525/534/550 words — still on target.

**[D1.2] fixed properly.** The tikz library moved to `p1/preamble.txt` and merged into `preamble.tex` after `\usepackage{tikz}`. I checked the consequence rather than the diff: page 1's memory map still draws both brace spans, so the library loads in its new position.

**[D1.1] withdrawn — that one was my mistake.** I reported that "reaching 25% at the 95th percentile" fused two of Pond's statements. It didn't. §3.1's body says verbatim: *"At the 95th percentile, stranding reaches 25% during high utilization periods."* In round 1 I matched the claim only against §3.1's closing summary bullet — which sits a page later and gives different numbers (3–27%, outliers 36%) — and never searched the body for the 25% itself. The sentence was correct and correctly sourced; I should not have flagged it.

**[D2.1], new, minor.** Acting on that bad call, the master replaced a correct sentence with one carrying a smaller error: "3–27% of it at the 95th percentile, **depending on the cluster**". The 3–27% range comes from Figure 2, whose x-axis is the percentage of scheduled CPU cores; each bucket pools snapshots from all 100 clusters. Pond reports no per-cluster stranding breakdown — Figure 2 is its only stranding figure — attributes within-bucket spread to "different VM mixes", and ties the top of the range to load. Reverting to the round-1 wording resolves it, or the trailing clause becomes something like "once most of a server's cores are booked".

That is one misattributed qualifier inside a 550-word summary, using the paper's own numbers, with nothing downstream depending on it. The substantive work — full coverage at 100 points, correct technical content, ~60 quotations checked in context against the six source PDFs, clean compile with legible figures — is intact. A minor defect alone is not grounds to withhold a pass.

VERDICT: PASS
